title: "The Human Visual System — Review"

# Evolution of visual systems

## Key timeline

| Species | Age (millions of years) | Particularity |
|--------|------------------------|---------------|
| Nautilus belauensis | ~450 | Pinhole eye, without lens |
| Octopus | ~200 | Flexible lens, contrast/motion detection |
| Reptiles | ~200 | Slit pupil, fine light control |
| Spiders | ~130 | Multi-eyes, differentiated functions |
| Birds | ~155 | Acuity > human, sometimes 2 foveas |
| Mammals | ~125 | Stereoscopic vision, depth perception |
| Homo sapiens | ~3 | Binocular frontal vision |

## Stages of evolution of the eye

1. Photosensitive spot → no direction
2. Depressed area → limited directional sensitivity
3. Pinhole eye → blurred but directional image
4. Closed chamber → transparent fluid
5. Developed lens → focus
6. Separate iris + cornea → complete vertebrate eye

# Historical theories of vision

## Chronology of theories

| Author | Date | Theory |
|--------|------|---------|
| Plato | 350 BC AD | **Extromissive**: the eye emits light |
| Aristotle | 330 BC AD | Material images carried by air |
| Alhazen | 1040 | **Intromissive**: the light goes towards the eye |
| Ptolemy | 150 BC AD | Known refraction phenomenon |
| Kepler | 1571–1630 | Retinal theory, image formed on the retina |

::: {.callout-warning title="Classic trap"}
The **extromissive** theories (the eye emits) are false. It is Alhazen who reverses the paradigm: objects send light towards the eye.
:::

## Contributions from Alhazen

- Self-luminous body (sun, moon, flame)
- Light in straight lines
- Irradiation in all directions
- Transparent/opaque media
- Pointillist theory + image geometry

## Modern theories — 3 currents

- **Psychology of perception** → features
- **Neurophysiology** → mechanistic explanations
- **Computational Vision** → new problems

# Characteristics of HVS

## Summary table

| Property | Value |
|-----------|--------|
| Visual Acuity | 20/20 ≈ 1 arc minute |
| Horizontal field (Field of View) | ~200° (120° binocular + 40° monocular ×2) |
| Vertical field | ~135° |
| Temporal resolution | ~60Hz |
| Instantaneous dynamic range | 6.5 f-stops (~5 orders of magnitude) |
| Adapted dynamic range | 46.5 f-stops (~14 orders of magnitude) |
| Accommodation | ~8 cm → ∞ (young) / ~50 cm → ∞ (50 years old) |
| Color | CIE xy space; linear distances in CIE Lab |

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap"}
Current displays cover only ~3 orders of magnitude vs ~14 for the adapted eye → hence HDR techniques.
:::

# Eye Anatomy

## Key structures

| Structure | Role |
|-----------|------|
| Cornea | ~70% of total refraction |
| Lens | Accommodation (variable curvature) |
| Iris | Diaphragm — controls the pupil |
| Retina | Photoreceptor layer |
| Fovea | High resolution zone (max cone density) |
| Optic disc | Optic nerve output = **blind spot** |
| Optic nerve | Signal → brain |
| Watery/glassy humor | Light transmission, eye shape |

---

# The Retina

## Organization

**3 layers** (from inside to outside):

1. Retinal Ganglion Cells (RGC) — innermost
2. Collecting cells — bipolar, horizontal, amacrine
3. Photoreceptors — cones + rods — outermost

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap"}
Light passes through layers 1 and 2 **before** reaching the photoreceptors → “inverted” eye relative to a camera.
:::

## Cones vs Sticks

| Property | Cones | Rods |
|-----------|--------------|-----------------|
| Number | ~10⁷ | ~10⁸ |
| Photopic | Bright light | Scotopic | Low light |
| Color | Yes (3 types) | No (grayscale) |
| Resolution | High | Low |
| Convergence | Limited | Strong |
| Location | Fovea | Periphery |

## The 3 types of cones

| Type | Wavelength | Color |
|------|-----------------|---------|
| S (Shorts) | ~419nm | Blue |
| M (Medium) | ~531nm | Green (dominant) |
| L (Long) | ~559nm | Red |

::: {.callout-note title="To remember"}
A rod after dark adaptation can respond to **a single photon**.
:::

## Distribution on the retina

- **Fovea**: max density of cones, almost no rods
- **Periphery**: dominant rods (peak ~15–20° eccentricity)
- **Optic disc**: no photoreceptor → blind spot

## Limitations of the eye

- Blood vessels in front of photoreceptors
- Retinal image **inverted** (corrected by the brain)
- High resolution only in **fovea**
- Blind spot
- Non-uniform brightness

---

# Retinal Ganglion Cells (RGC)

## Role

Replace absolute brightness levels with a **difference map** (retinotopic map of differences).

## Center-Surround Organization

- **On-center / Off-surround**: activated if light in the center
- **Off-center / On-surround**: activated if there is light around

→ Amplification of **local contrasts** without representing absolute values.

## M vs P cells

| Property | M (Magnocellulars) | P (Parvocellular) |
|-----------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Input | Large number of photoreceptors | Small number |
| Spatial resolution | Low | High |
| Temporal resolution | High | Low |
| Color | No | Yes |
| Cell size | Large | Small |
| Conduction speed | Fast | Slow |
| Role | Motion, rapid detection | Color, texture, objects |
| LGN Channel | Magnocellular (2 layers) | Parvocellular (4 layers) |

---

# Oculomotor Processes

## Accommodation

- **Far vision**: ciliary muscles relaxed → lens flattened
- **Close vision**: contracted ciliary muscles → bulging lens
- Decreases with age → **presbyopia**

## Depth indices

| Type | Cue oculomotor | Cue visual |
|------|-----------------|-----------|
| Binocular (Stereopsis) | Vergence | Binocular disparity |
| Monocular | Accommodation | Retinal Blur |

## Refractive errors

| Condition | Problem | Correction |
|-----------|----------|------------|
| Emmetropia | Normal | None |
| Myopia (Myopia) | Focus before the retina | Concave lens |
| Hyperopia (Hypermetropia) | Focus behind the retina | Convex lens |
| Astigmatism | No single household | Cylindrical lens |

# Visual Cortex

## Visual pathway — Pipeline
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    R[Rétine] --> NO[Nerf optique\nOptic Nerve]
    NO --> CO[Chiasma optique\nOptic Chiasm]
    CO --> LGN[LGN\nNoyau Géniculé Latéral]
    LGN --> V1[Cortex V1\nPrimaire]
    V1 --> VS[Flux ventral\nWhat]
    V1 --> DS[Flux dorsal\nWhere]
```

::: {.callout-note title="To remember"}
Visual field **left** → hemisphere **right** (and vice versa) — decussation at the chiasm.
:::

## LGN (Lateral Geniculate Nucleus)

- 1 LGN per hemisphere
- **2 magnocellular layers** ← M cells → temporal resolution
- **4 parvocellular layers** ← P cells → spatial resolution + color
- All layers maintain **retinotopy**

## V1 — 3 types of cells (Hubel & Wiesel, Nobel Prize 1981)

| Type | Property |
|------|-----------|
| Center-Perimeter | Detection of contrasting light points |
| Simple Cells | Edges oriented to specific position and orientation |
| Complexes (Complex Cells) | Oriented edges, partial position tolerance |

**Hierarchy**: Center-Perimeter → Simple → Complex

## Hypercolumns

Spatial organization of V1 minimizing the distance between neurons coding:

- The original eye (left/right)
- Preferred orientation
- Retinotopic localization

**Hebb's rule**: neurons that fire together wire together.

## Contrast Sensitivity Function (CSF)

- Peak at **4–6 cpd** (cycles per degree)
- High frequency decay (limit ~60 cpd)
- Decay at low frequencies (lateral inhibition)
- Moves according to **viewing distance**

## Dorsal vs Ventral Flow

| Feed | Management | Function | Areas |
|------|-----------|----------|-------|
| **Ventral** (What) | V1 → V4 → IT temporal | Recognition of objects, color, identity | V1, V2, V4, TEO, TE |
| **Dorsal** (Where) | V1 → MT → Parietal | Location, movement | V1, V2, V3, MT/MST |

## Progression along the ventral flow

| Area | RF (°) | Latency (ms) | Invariance |
|------|--------|-------------|------------|
| NGL | 1 | — | None |
| V1 | 1 | 40–60 | Zero position |
| V2 | 1.4 | 50–70 | — |
| V4 | 4.8 | 60–80 | Color, shape |
| TEO | 5.8 | 70–90 | View-dependent |
| TE | 12 | 80–100 | **View-independent** |

## Specialized areas

- **FFA** (Fusiform Face Area) → faces
- **PPA** (Parahippocampal Place Area) → places, scenes

# Computational Models Inspired by HVS

## From organic to artificial

| Organic | Artificial |
|------------|-----------|
| Simple cells V1 (orientations) | Convolutional filters, SIFT, HOG |
| Complex cells (spatial pooling) | Max-pooling |
| Simple → complex hierarchy | CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks) |
| Ventral flow feedforward | Deep architectures |

## Neocognitron (Fukushima)

- 1st network inspired by Hubel & Wiesel
- Alternating layers S (simple) and C (complex)
- Translation invariant → precursor of CNNs

## LeNet (LeCun et al., 1998)

- Backpropagation learning
- Architecture: Conv → Pool → Conv → Pool → Dense → Dense → Output
- Applied to digit recognition (MNIST)

::: {.callout-warning title="Known limit"}
The actual ventral flow is **bidirectional** with significant feedback connections — not yet fully exploited in computer vision.
:::

# Applications

## Stereoscopic Displays

- Principle: present a **slightly different** image to each eye
- Exploits **binocular disparity**
- Wheatstone (1838) → modern 3D glasses (176 years later)

## Virtual Reality (VR/AR)

| Generation | Technology | Actors |
|------------|-------------|---------|
| 1838 | Stereoscopes | Wheatstone, Brewster |
| 1968 | Pioneering VR | Ivan Sutherland |
| 2012–now | VR explosion | Meta, Apple, Sony |

**Advanced technologies**:

- Gaze-Contingent Focus Displays (eye-tracking + variable optics)
- Near-eye Light Field Displays
- Holographic Displays (full wavefront)

## Vergence-Accommodation Conflict

::: {.callout-warning title="Critical point"}
In classic stereo displays: eyes **converge** towards the perceived 3D position but **accommodate** on the physical screen → inevitable conflict.
:::

**Effects**: visual discomfort, fatigue, nausea, double vision, pathologies in children.

**Comfort zone**: depends on the viewing distance (cinema > TV > desktop > mobile).

| Condition | Real world | Classic stereo display |
|-----------|------------|--------------------------|
| Vergence | Object distance | Object distance (simulated) |
| Accommodation | Object distance | **screen distance** (fixed) |
| Result | ✅ Match | ❌ Mismatch |
